subject.title: fix(gateway): bound connect frame auth.* fields at the protocol schema

question: Should connect-frame auth schema hardening enforce byte-level or strict token-shape limits now, and what permanent limits are acceptable for operator-configured shared-secret fields?
rationale: The patch changes a gateway pre-auth security boundary and protocol compatibility contract; automation can identify the byte/grapheme gap, but maintainers need to accept the durable auth-field limits or narrow the scope.

options.title: Require byte-safe documented caps
options.body: Have the branch enforce byte-length or strict token alphabet bounds across all six auth fields, add byte-heavy tests, and document the accepted protocol limits before merge.

options.title: Narrow generated-token hardening
options.body: Cap only bootstrap/device-style generated tokens now, then split shared-secret and runtime-token policy into a separately reviewed protocol decision.

options.title: Pause for broader protocol policy
options.body: Hold this PR until gateway/security owners decide a general connect-frame size and shape policy for all auth-bearing fields.

recommendation.title: Require byte-safe documented caps
recommendation.body: Have the branch enforce byte-length or strict token alphabet bounds across all six auth fields, add byte-heavy tests, and document the accepted protocol limits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the strongest repeated ownership signal across the gateway auth/protocol and security helper surfaces implicated by the decision.
